title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space
summary: Tomas Mikolov, Kai Chen, Greg Corrado, and Jeffrey Dean submitted 'Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space' on January 16, 2013, proposing two model architectures for learning continuous word representations from large datasets: Continuous Bag-of-Words (CBOW) and Skip-gram.
significance: A documented natural-language-processing research milestone establishing computationally efficient CBOW and Skip-gram architectures for learning continuous word vectors at large scale.

verification.note: The original arXiv record establishes the January 16, 2013 first-submission date, authors, and the proposal of two architectures for computing continuous word representations from very large datasets. Google Research independently corroborates the title, authors, 2013 ICLR publication context, and the core abstract claims. This record uses the arXiv submission date strictly as a research-publication milestone. It does not claim this date as the release date of software named word2vec, the invention of word embeddings generally, or a causal ancestor of later NLP systems. No geography, affiliation, ancestry, influence, causality, or relationships are inferred.
